findings.title: Partial recovery marks a whole resolution filed before History and task effects complete
findings.evidence: Every pending resolution becomes filed at plan:9756 immediately after the CRM phase. History runs at 9758-9779 and tasks at 9781-9795. If create_task or escalation later fails, _persist_partial stores all those filed resolutions at 9702-9708. The retry merges them as complete and computes pending=[], returning at 9635-9638, so missing tasks are never created. If the second CRM contact fails, the first contact's distinct page can likewise be skipped forever. The existing test only proves the first CRM call is not replayed; it never asserts completion of all page/task effects.
findings.fix: Track completion per effect or per resolution-stage, not with one filed bit set before downstream effects. Persist landed CRM/page/task tokens and retry every absent required effect idempotently; add failures after distinct-page History and after the first task, then assert the next run completes every missing effect without duplicating landed ones.

findings.title: Budget exit records spend but discards the paid extraction cache
findings.evidence: extract raises BudgetExceeded carrying the stamped extraction, but the handler at 9880-9893 writes only cost_usd and model_receipt into run-receipt.json. No ObservationRow is appended with exc.extraction. A retry with the same source_ref/digest/slugs cannot find the cache and makes another paid call, violating FR-001 and the interface comment that paid extraction is persisted first.
findings.fix: Carry the active message identity, resolutions and context into the budget handler or catch BudgetExceeded inside _file_message; append a non-terminal partial ledger row containing exc.extraction before returning exit 12. Add a retry test asserting zero additional Claude calls.

findings.title: A simulated revision loses revision_of on the later real run
findings.evidence: On the dry-run of a changed digest, revision_of is the old digest and the simulated row records it. On the later live run, ledger.latest is that simulated row with the new digest, so plan:9616 makes same_digest_prior non-null and 9617 sets revision_of=None. The live History entry at 9765 is therefore unmarked, and the real ledger row at 9803-9808 loses supersede propagation. The dry/live test covers only a first filing, not a revision.
findings.fix: When same_digest_prior is simulated or partial, carry forward its revision_of. Add dry-run revision -> live revision coverage asserting the actual page and live ledger retain the old digest marker.

findings.title: The G4 item-3 checker rejects legitimate producer blocks
findings.evidence: The checker requires extraction, quote, CRM, page, task and digest lines for every preview block at 13299-13313. The actual ignored/escalated path calls plan_message_preview with extraction=None and empty effect lists at 9655-9659. A normal real-inbox dry-run containing any unknown or ambiguous sender therefore fails G4 despite correct behavior. Valid filed extractions with no decisions/commitments/questions also lack a quote and task line. The real-producer positive fixture contains only one specially rich filed message, so it does not expose this mismatch.
findings.fix: Make the preview contract explicit for absent sections, such as extraction: n/a, CRM: none, page: none and task: none, or condition checker requirements on resolution outcome. Generate positive fixtures containing filed-with-empty-items, ignored and escalated messages, and require all to pass.

findings.title: G4 still accepts an unbound G1 record and an unevidenced verification floor
findings.evidence: check1 validates suite.sha only; it never requires rec.sha/base_sha or equality with the tested tree. The positive g1-record fixture deliberately has no SHA. check_8_floor at 13599-13633 accepts Layer 1/Layer 3 text plus any three operational filenames and never requires the Opus G0 artifact, Codex review/challenge artifacts, FINAL/Fable artifact, verify-review-artifact results or gate-invocation records named by the goal. This can produce a false GREEN release matrix.
findings.fix: Require the G1 record's measured tree SHA and bind it to an immutable tree-equivalent commit/merge receipt. Define and validate the exact required Layer-1 and Layer-3 artifact paths and successful gate records, with one negative fixture per required artifact.

findings.title: The lease heartbeat is not time-bounded during sweep or message processing
findings.evidence: The binding A2 decision requires heartbeat touch every 10 minutes or less, especially for backfills. The only touch is once before each message at 9848-9850. gmail_source.sweep runs first with no heartbeat and may perform a full query plus up to 14 daily calls, each through a runner whose default timeout is 120 seconds. A single message's read, extraction and multiple writes also have no periodic heartbeat. The 60-minute lease can therefore be declared stale while the original run is active.
findings.fix: Add a real periodic heartbeat covering the entire acquired interval, including sweep and long per-message work, and stop immediately if it detects loss. Test with a controllable clock/heartbeat callback across a simulated long sweep and long extraction.

findings.title: coverage-diff treats a missing old-path input as zero historical coverage
findings.evidence: load_jsonl returns [] when its path does not exist, and main at 14424-14442 then writes a successful report with zero candidates. FR-006 makes this report the prerequisite for deleting the old ingest path; accepting a missing source file can falsely certify no coverage losses.
findings.fix: Fail nonzero when --old-interactions, the ledger, or required CRM inputs are missing/unreadable or malformed. Add a missing-input negative test and require a non-empty/explicitly-accounted old-path window before the activation gate can pass.

findings.title: write_interaction accepts proof for the wrong Gmail source
findings.evidence: The validator requires source_ref to exist and verifies contact_id, but never compares parsed source_ref with gmail:<msg.id>. A stale or malformed success object for the correct contact but another message is accepted and the orchestrator records the current effect as filed.
findings.fix: Require parsed['source_ref'] == f'gmail:{msg.id}' as well as the expected contact_id. Add a wrong-source regression and point a mutation row at the equality guard.

findings.title: Mutation cleanup can finish green after final restoration fails
findings.evidence: restore_all detects failed copies and preserves backups, but returns 0 at 15040-15045. If every mutation row passed and only the EXIT-trap restoration fails, the prior exit status is zero and the harness may still report success while leaving a target mutated. This contradicts the stated fail-closed discipline.
findings.fix: Make restoration failure override the final status, for example with an EXIT handler that captures the original rc, performs restore, and exits nonzero if any restore failed. Add an intentional restore-failure selftest.

findings.title: Task 1 still materialises the superseded FakeRunner contract
findings.evidence: The Task-1 block at 576-634 says every matching response is consumed and executes del self.responses[i]. The corrected consume-only-if-followed implementation does not appear until Task 7 at 3804-3880, although the canonical interface says Task 1 owns this fake. The final tree is correct and downstream gates pass, but an implementation stopped or reviewed at Task 1 receives a contract-violating module.
findings.fix: Put the corrected FakeRunner implementation in Task 1 and repeat that same version in Task 7's whole-file restatement. Re-run the through-1 and through-2 task gates.

findings.title: Lease release failures are silently reported as successful runs
findings.evidence: Lease.release invokes meeting-brief-release but ignores returncode. run writes a success receipt and returns exit 0 before finally calling release at 9912-9913. A failed release leaves the lock active for up to its TTL while the receipt claims success, causing subsequent polls to refuse without surfacing the original release failure.
findings.fix: Check release rc and persist a dedicated failure diagnostic or convert the run to exit 3 without overwriting the last successful timestamp. Add nonzero-release and timeout tests.

rejected_as_locked: FakeRunner consume-only-if-followed, last-response-sticky semantics are the integrator's locked C1 decision; no finding reopens that behavior.
Simulated rows with planned_writes are intentionally non-terminal and do not count as real CRM coverage; this is the locked dry-run decision.
Cached matches are re-resolved through the stored extraction context without triggering a new LLM call; the at-most-one-call identity remains locked.
Lease loss is intentionally a stop condition and release becomes a no-op after loss; no finding requests fail-open continuation.
CLIENT_STATE_REPO_ROOT being mandatory for G1 and mutation-check is locked and correctly fail-closed.
The cortextos shim's exact pass-through set is meeting-brief-claim, meeting-brief-release and read-only list-tasks; requesting that list-tasks be trapped would contradict the amended goal.
A lock-held run intentionally leaves run-receipt.json byte-identical and writes last-lock-refusal.json; requiring the ordinary second successful run's receipt to remain unchanged is rejected.
